title: AI-Efficient Language Guide
purpose: Defines the controlled vocabulary, abbreviation dictionary, tag taxonomy, and token-efficient writing conventions for this repository. Every file should minimize boilerplate and use canonical terms only. Addresses the A1-Alpha finding of same-concept-different-names across the repo and think-tank-beta's token cost analysis showing 57% index bloat from derived data and redundant keys.

section_1_controlled_vocabulary.title: Canonical Terms for This Repository
section_1_controlled_vocabulary.description: Use ONLY the preferred term. Never use the discouraged synonyms. Zero-synonym policy: one concept, one word.

terms.context: Use in indexes, cross-references, and documentation.

terms.definition: A discrete piece of knowledge produced by a team during a session.
terms.context: Use in team outputs, think tank reports, and KB entries.

terms.context: Use in session logs, attribution fields, and coordination.

terms.context: Use when referring to individual agents within a team.

terms.context: Use in team logs and performance tracking.

terms.context: Use in multi_team_runner plans and coordinator instructions.

section_2_abbreviation_dictionary.title: Standard Abbreviations
section_2_abbreviation_dictionary.description: Use these abbreviations in filenames, path references, comments, and compact headers. Always expand in titles and prose meant for human reading.

section_3_tag_taxonomy.title: Normalized Tag Taxonomy
section_3_tag_taxonomy.description: All tags MUST be kebab-case, from this controlled list. Maximum 5 tags per entry. Tags must not duplicate the entry's category.

rules.rationale: More than 5 tags dilutes specificity and increases index token cost.

rules.rule: Tags must be from the taxonomy above
rules.rationale: A1-Alpha found 149 unique tags with overlapping synonyms (e.g., 'sops' vs 'SOPs' vs 'sop-improvements'). The taxonomy reduces this to ~45 normalized terms.
rules.extension: New tags may be added to the taxonomy by updating this SOP. Do not invent ad-hoc tags.

rules.rule: Tags must not duplicate the category
Use the most specific tag available

section_4_categories.title: Fixed Category List
section_4_categories.description: Every indexed entry has exactly one category from this list. Categories are mutually exclusive.

section_5_path_references.title: Path Reference Format
section_5_path_references.description: When referencing files in documentation, use the shortest unambiguous path.

rules.rule: Use shortest unambiguous path from repo root
rules.example_best: sops/sop_029_file_naming.json (if context makes the parent clear)

rules.rule: For cross-references between entries, use the ID not the path
rules.rationale: IDs are shorter (7 tokens vs 15+ tokens for a full path) and survive renames.

rules.evidence: A1-Alpha found SCR-0029 through SCR-0033 using relative paths (../) in scripts/index.json. These break when the index is read from a different working directory.
rules.fix: Use paths relative to repo root, never relative to the current file.

rules.rule: In index.json, the 'file' field is filename only
rules.rationale: The directory is implicit from the index location. Adding it wastes tokens.

section_6_token_budget_awareness.title: Token-Efficient Writing Conventions
section_6_token_budget_awareness.description: Every file should minimize boilerplate without sacrificing clarity.

guidelines.guideline: Put the most important information first
guidelines.rationale: Agents that read only the first N tokens of a file should get the highest-value content. Summaries before details. Findings before methodology. Recommendations before evidence.
guidelines.evidence: Think-tank-beta A1-TC03: mandatory summary in first 500 bytes saves 80% of wasted reads.

guidelines.guideline: Use IDs for cross-references, not titles or descriptions
guidelines.example_bad: Builds on the 'Anti-Recursion Protocol: Preventing Inward-Facing Gravity' SOP

guidelines.guideline: Avoid redundant metadata in JSON files
guidelines.rationale: The 'sop_' prefix on every key is redundant when the file is already in the sops/ directory.

guidelines.guideline: Use arrays instead of objects for tabular data
guidelines.rationale: Think-tank-beta A1-TC04: 31 entries repeating 9 keys each = 560 tokens of pure key repetition. For bulk data, consider header+rows format.
guidelines.note: Standard JSON with named keys is preferred for < 20 entries. Header+rows only for large datasets.

guidelines.rationale: 10-12 lines of YAML frontmatter per KB entry costs ~30 tokens. Across 31 entries, 930 tokens of boilerplate. Keep frontmatter to essential fields only.
guidelines.remove: Fields duplicated in the index (title is in both frontmatter and index -- keep in both as it aids standalone reading)

guidelines.guideline: Do not repeat information available in the index
guidelines.example_bad: A KB entry that lists all related entries with their full titles and dates
guidelines.example_good: builds_on: [KB-0008, KB-0015] (let the reader look up titles in the index if needed)

section_7_anti_patterns.title: Anti-Patterns to Avoid
section_7_anti_patterns.description: Common token-wasting patterns found in the repository.

anti_patterns.name: Verbose frontmatter
anti_patterns.description: YAML frontmatter with inline comments, multi-line descriptions, or fields that belong in the body.
anti_patterns.example_bad:
---
id: KB-0032
title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Storage Patterns and Their Implications for Multi-Agent Systems  # This entry analyzes...
description: |
  This knowledge base entry provides a detailed examination of
  various storage patterns...
---
anti_patterns.example_good:
---
id: KB-0032
date: 2026-03-11
team: TEAM-0030
category: architecture
tags: [database, caching, optimization]
status: validated
---

anti_patterns.name: Redundant JSON keys with type prefixes
anti_patterns.description: Prefixing every key with the object type when context already provides it.
anti_patterns.savings: ~3-5 tokens per key, compounds across large files

anti_patterns.name: Derived data stored alongside source data
anti_patterns.description: Storing tag_index, categories, by_data_type alongside the entries they are derived from.
anti_patterns.evidence: A1-Alpha: knowledge-base/index.json has tag_index (3,500 tokens) fully derivable from entries[].tags

anti_patterns.name: Full paths instead of IDs in cross-references
anti_patterns.description: Using file paths where an ID reference would suffice.

anti_patterns.name: Repetitive boilerplate sections
anti_patterns.description: KB entries with empty or template-text sections that add no information.
anti_patterns.example_bad:
## Lessons Learned

No additional lessons beyond those stated above.

## Recommendations

See the recommendations in the Result section.
anti_patterns.example_good: Omit empty sections entirely. Only include sections with substantive content.

anti_patterns.name: Inconsistent synonyms across files
anti_patterns.description: Using 'entry' in one file and 'record' in another for the same concept.
anti_patterns.evidence: A1-Alpha: 'team' vs 'added_by_team' vs 'populated_by' across different indexes
anti_patterns.fix: Use section_1 controlled vocabulary. One concept, one word.

anti_patterns.name: Large files without summaries
anti_patterns.description: Files >2000 tokens that require reading the entire content to determine relevance.
anti_patterns.evidence: Five KB entries exceed 25KB (167KB total). Agents reading them to check relevance waste ~42,000 tokens.
anti_patterns.fix: Per SOP-029 SIZE-01, add summary in first 500 bytes.

before_writing_any_file: All terms match the controlled vocabulary in section_1
Tags are from the taxonomy in section_3 (max 5, kebab-case)
Category is from the fixed list in section_4
Cross-references use IDs not paths (section_5 PATH-02)
No redundant type prefixes on JSON keys (section_7 AP-02)
Summary present if file >2000 tokens (section_7 AP-07)
